  2. The log ends with a summary of the model and the evaluation.
  3. The bar at the bottom of the dock keeps the key numbers in view, for example presence=116 background=10,108 | train AUC=0.9135 | CV AUC=0.7524.

The test AUC from spatial cross-validation is lower than the training AUC. That gap is normal and honest: it shows how well the model does in places it was not fitted to (Roberts et al. 2017).

docs.title: Part 4. Read the results and make the map (④ Results)
Step 10. Look at the response curves
docs.text:
Click the ④ Results tab.

  1. The Response Curves sub-tab is open.
  2. Choose a variable in Variable.
  3. The curve shows how predicted suitability changes along that variable. The shaded band is the range of values at the training points.

docs.title: Step 11. See which variables matter
docs.text:
1. Click Jackknife Importance.
  2. The left panel shows the ROC curves. The right panel compares the model fitted with only one variable and without that variable.
  1. Permutation Importance ranks the variables by how much the model gets worse when each one is shuffled.
  2. Save PNG... saves the chart.
  3. Save CSV... saves the numbers.

docs.title: Step 12. Make the suitability map
docs.text:
1. Click Spatial Projection.
  2. Keep cloglog in Output transform. It gives values from 0 to 1 that read as relative suitability (Phillips et al. 2017).
  3. Output raster is where the map is saved. Click ... to change it.
  4. Click ▶ Run Spatial Projection.
  1. When the status line reads Done: followed by the file path, the map is saved and added to the project.
  1. The prediction layer appears in the Layers panel. Darker colours mean higher predicted suitability.

docs.title: Part 5. Pick survey sites (⑤ Survey Site Selection)
Step 13. Set up the survey
docs.text:
Click the ⑤ Survey Site Selection tab.

  1. Survey purpose: choose High-suitability search to look for new populations in places that are suitable but not yet surveyed.
  2. High-suitability search settings: Minimum suitability is the lowest map value a site may have.
  3. Sampling strategy: set how many sites you want and how far apart they must be from known records and from each other (in metres).
  4. Click ▶ Select Survey Sites.

docs.title: Step 14. Check the survey sites
docs.text:
1. The status line reports the result, for example ✓ 20 survey sites selected (MinSuit = 0.9000), and where the GeoPackage was saved.
  1. The Survey sites layer is added on top of the map. Open its attribute table to see the coordinates, the suitability value and, if reverse geocoding was on, the address of each site.

docs.title: What you have done
docs.text: In these steps you ran a complete species distribution modelling workflow inside QGIS. You loaded presence points and environmental rasters, checked that the rasters line up, fitted a regularized Maxent model, evaluated it with spatial cross-validation, read the response curves and variable importance, mapped habitat suitability and turned the map into a list of field survey sites.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Read the User guide chapters to learn what each control does and when to change its default.
  • Work through the Bradypus worked example for a closer reading of every plot.
  • Practise fixing rasters that do not line up with the Ariolimax example.
  • Reproduce a published study with the Pitta nympha example.

docs.title: References
docs.text: QMaxent's defaults, evaluation procedures, and survey-planning workflows are grounded in the species distribution modeling (SDM) literature. This chapter groups the works the plugin draws on by topic, with a one-line annotation on how each reference is used inside QMaxent. The plugin source code carries inline citations to these works in the relevant modules (workers/maxent_worker.py, bridge/elapid_bridge.py, bridge/priority_sites.py, core/venv_manager.py).

docs.title: Maxent — core methodology
docs.text:
Phillips, S. J., Anderson, R. P., & Schapire, R. E. (2006). Maximum entropy modeling of species geographic distributions. Ecological Modelling, 190(3-4), 231–259. The original Maxent paper. QMaxent's feature-class taxonomy (LQPHT), jackknife importance, and ROC-based evaluation all come from this formulation.

Phillips, S. J., & Dudík, M. (2008). Modeling of species distributions with Maxent: new extensions and a comprehensive evaluation. Ecography, 31(2), 161–175. The benchmark paper behind the maxent.jar sample-size feature-class rule (used by QMaxent's Auto mode up to v0.1.x) and the regularization-multiplier default of 1.0.

Phillips, S. J., Anderson, R. P., Dudík, M., Schapire, R. E., & Blair, M. E. (2017). Opening the black box: an open-source release of Maxent. Ecography, 40(7), 887–893. The release of the open-source Maxent and the maxnet R package, and the formal recommendation to adopt the cloglog output transform, adopted as QMaxent's default. Since v0.2.0, QMaxent's "Auto (maxnet default rule by sample size)" mode follows the maxnet default feature classes (maxnet.formula(classes = "default")).

Fithian, W., & Hastie, T. (2013). Finite-sample equivalence in statistical models for presence-only data. The Annals of Applied Statistics, 7(4), 1917–1939. The paper that establishes the formal equivalence between Maxent and infinitely-weighted logistic regression — the foundation for elapid's implementation.

docs.title: elapid — software backend
docs.text:
Anderson, C. B. (2023). elapid: Species distribution modeling tools for Python. Journal of Open Source Software, 8(84), 5435. The peer-reviewed release of the elapid library that QMaxent uses for its MaxentModel, GeographicKFold, and feature transformers.

Pedregosa, F., et al. (2011). Scikit-learn: Machine learning in Python. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 12, 2825–2830. The numerical core that elapid's regularized-likelihood maximisation delegates to.

Harris, C. R., et al. (2020). Array programming with NumPy. Nature, 585, 357–362. The array library underlying elapid, scikit-learn, and the QMaxent raster-extraction layer.

docs.title: Plugin architecture
docs.text: Wu, Q. (2026). GeoAI: A Python package for integrating artificial intelligence with geospatial data analysis and visualization. Journal of Open Source Software, 11(118), 9605. https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.09605 The QGIS plugin from which QMaxent's dependency-installation workflow in core/venv_manager.py was adapted — in particular the _get_qgis_python() pattern that resolves the real Python interpreter on Windows (where sys.executable points to qgis-bin.exe) and the subprocess pipe handling used during pip install.

docs.title: Cross-validation and model evaluation
docs.text:
Roberts, D. R., et al. (2017). Cross-validation strategies for data with temporal, spatial, hierarchical, or phylogenetic structure. Ecography, 40(8), 913–929. The paper that established spatial cross-validation as the default for SDMs — directly shaping QMaxent's Geographic K-Fold default and the warning text in The Parameters tab.

Hijmans, R. J. (2012). Cross-validation of species distribution models: removing spatial sorting bias and calibration with a null model. Ecology, 93(3), 679–688. Provides the formal argument for buffered leave-one-out CV when sample sizes are small; QMaxent's *Buffered LOO option implements this.*

Valavi, R., Elith, J., Lahoz-Monfort, J. J., & Guillera-Arroita, G. (2019). blockCV: An R package for generating spatially or environmentally separated folds for k-fold cross-validation of species distribution models. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 10(2), 225–232. The block-CV recipes implemented by QMaxent's Checkerboard option.

Muscarella, R., et al. (2014). ENMeval: An R package for conducting spatially independent evaluations and estimating optimal model complexity for Maxent ecological niche models. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 5(11), 1198–1205. The hyperparameter-tuning framework whose checkerboard partitioning is implemented as a QMaxent CV option.

Kass, J. M., et al. (2018). Wallace: A flexible platform for reproducible modeling of species niches and distributions built for community expansion. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 9(4), 1151–1156. The interactive ENM platform whose hyperparameter-tuning workflow QMaxent intentionally complements rather than duplicates.

docs.title: Sample bias correction
docs.text:
Phillips, S. J., et al. (2009). Sample selection bias and presence-only distribution models: implications for background and pseudo-absence data. Ecological Applications, 19(1), 181–197. The paper underlying QMaxent's *Down-weight spatially clustered points option in the Parameters → Advanced section.*

Boria, R. A., Olson, L. E., Goodman, S. M., & Anderson, R. P. (2014). Spatial filtering to reduce sampling bias can improve the performance of ecological niche models. Ecological Modelling, 275, 73–77. Cited in Data tab as the reason to spatially-thin presence layers before modeling.

Elith, J., Kearney, M., & Phillips, S. (2010). The art of modelling range-shifting species. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 1(4), 330–342. The MESS-style extrapolation analysis whose logic underlies QMaxent's unified projection-preflight dialog.

docs.title: SDM best-practice reviews
docs.text:
Elith, J., et al. (2011). A statistical explanation of MaxEnt for ecologists. Diversity and Distributions, 17(1), 43–57. The standard pedagogical reference for understanding what Maxent does and does not assume.

Merow, C., Smith, M. J., & Silander Jr, J. A. (2013). A practical guide to MaxEnt for modeling species' distributions: what it does, and why inputs and settings matter. Ecography, 36(10), 1058–1069. The companion practical guide to Elith et al. 2011.

Araújo, M. B., et al. (2019). Standards for distribution models in biodiversity assessments. Science Advances, 5(1), eaat4858. The IPBES-aligned reporting standard QMaxent's XLSX export was designed to satisfy. Cited throughout this manual.

Radosavljevic, A., & Anderson, R. P. (2014). Making better Maxent models of species distributions: complexity, overfitting and evaluation. Journal of Biogeography, 41(4), 629–643. The empirical paper documenting how feature-class tuning without spatial CV inflates AUC, and that the best settings depend on the data; underlies the advice in the Parameters tab to treat the Auto rule as a default and compare alternatives.

docs.title: Survey design
docs.text:
Williams, J. N., et al. (2009). Using species distribution models to predict new occurrences for rare plants. Diversity and Distributions, 15(4), 565–576. The original survey-design paper behind the *High-suitability search mode of the Survey Site Selection tab.*

Rhoden, C. M., Peterman, W. E., & Taylor, C. A. (2017). Maxent- directed field surveys identify new populations of narrowly endemic habitat specialists. PeerJ, 5, e3632. The model-validation companion to Williams et al. 2009; QMaxent's *Gradient-stratified sampling mode (equal numbers of sites from four suitability quartiles) reproduces this design.*

Stevens, D. L. Jr., & Olsen, A. R. (2004). Spatially balanced sampling of natural resources. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 99(465), 262–278. The spatially-balanced-sampling theory underlying QMaxent's between-candidate spacing constraint.

Robinson, N. M., et al. (2018). Refining survey effort: how detection probability shapes the design of biodiversity surveys. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 9(3), 575–587. Cited in Survey Site Selection for typical survey-budget heuristics.

docs.title: Worked example reference
docs.text: Lee, S.-J., et al. (2025). Breeding habitat prediction and nest-site characteristics of the fairy pitta (Pitta nympha) in Geoje-si, South Korea — Insights from a species distribution model. Global Ecology and Conservation, 64, e03939. The published Java-MaxEnt analysis reproduced in the Pitta nympha worked example.

docs.title: How QMaxent cites itself
docs.text:
If you publish a study using QMaxent, please cite:

Yu, B.-H. (2026). QMaxent: Maxent species distribution modeling in QGIS. Software. https://github.com/osgeokr/qmaxent

The exact CITATION.cff is the canonical source on the repository.

docs.title: ④ Results tab
docs.text:
After a successful run, the Results tab unlocks four sub-tabs:

Sub-tab What it shows Response Curves How each variable shapes predicted suitability across its data range Jackknife Importance Which variables matter most, with ROC plotted alongside Permutation Importance AUC drop when each variable is shuffled, as % of the total; the data it is evaluated on is set by Evaluate on in ② Parameters Spatial Projection Write the prediction to a GeoTIFF and load it as a styled QGIS layer

docs.title: Step 1. Response curves
docs.text:
1. Click Response Curves.
  2. Choose a variable in Variable.
  3. Read the curve: how predicted suitability changes along that variable, with the training range shaded.

docs.title: Step 2. Variable importance
docs.text:
1. Click Jackknife Importance.
  2. The ROC curves (left) and the jackknife bars (right).
  1. Click Permutation Importance.
  2. Save PNG... saves the chart.
  3. Save CSV... saves the numbers.

docs.title: Step 3. Make the suitability map
docs.text:
1. Click Spatial Projection.
  2. Choose the Output transform (cloglog by default).
  3. Check the Output raster path.
  4. Click ▶ Run Spatial Projection.
  1. The progress bar.
  2. The current step.
  1. Done: and the path of the saved GeoTIFF.
  1. The map is added to the Layers panel when Auto-load result as QGIS layer is ticked.

docs.title: Response Curves
docs.text:
Pick a variable from the drop-down at the top. QMaxent draws the predicted cloglog suitability across the variable's actual training range (shaded band) with the mean as a vertical reference line:

For continuous variables the curve is a marginal-effect plot in the sense of Elith et al. 2011: suitability is computed at the sweep of values for the focal variable while every other variable is held at its mean (or, for categoricals, its modal level).

For categorical variables, QMaxent renders a bar chart with one bar per class, ordered by predicted suitability — visually clearer than the ramped curve a Java-MaxEnt run would produce.

The shaded Training range band is important: predictions outside this band are pure extrapolation. Whenever your eventual spatial projection reaches values outside the band, QMaxent shows a one-off Multivariate Environmental Similarity Surface-style warning (see Elith, Kearney & Phillips 2010) before writing the output GeoTIFF.

The grid view across all variables is the standard Phillips et al. 2006 summary plot used in publications. QMaxent saves it as prediction_response_curves.png (300 dpi) when the Save analysis charts as PNG checkbox is on at projection time — see Exporting results.

docs.title: Jackknife Importance
docs.text:
This sub-tab combines the ROC curve and per-variable Jackknife bars in a single panel — the canonical Maxent figure since Phillips, Anderson & Schapire 2006:

Reading the ROC panel:

  • Training ROC (solid) — in-sample fit
  • Mean CV ROC (dashed) — across-fold mean of held-out folds
  • Per-fold ROC (faint) — variance across folds is the model's spatial sub-sample stability

Reading the Jackknife bars:

  • With-only (dark) — AUC of a model fit on this variable alone
  • Without (light) — AUC of the full model with this variable removed
  • A variable with a high with-only and a high without drop carries a unique signal not redundant with the others (the most informative kind).

The bars are sorted by Test AUC drop by default. The same numbers are exported into Table 4 of the XLSX — see Exporting results for the sheet layout.

docs.title: Spatial Projection
docs.text:
The third sub-tab projects the trained model across all the input rasters, producing a habitat-suitability GeoTIFF.

Controls:

  • Output transform:
  • cloglog (default) — interpretable as probability of presence given a typical sample of the species, the form Phillips et al. 2017 recommend as the new default.
  • logistic — the older (Phillips & Dudík 2008) parameterisation; still used in some published baselines.
  • raw — the unnormalised exponential output, mostly useful for advanced post-processing.
  • Auto-load result as QGIS layer (default on) — the GeoTIFF appears on the canvas with a default white-to-green ramp.
  • Save analysis charts as PNG — when on, three additional 300-dpi PNGs (ROC, Jackknife, response-curve grid) are written next to the GeoTIFF. Sized for direct paste into a single-column manuscript figure.

docs.title: The unified preflight dialog
docs.text:
Before writing the projection, QMaxent runs two safety checks in a single combined dialog:

  1. Categorical-code coverage — any class code present in the projection rasters but unseen during training is auto-masked to NoData (rather than silently extrapolated to a random class probability). As a further safeguard, since v0.2.0 the projection no longer fails if such a class still reaches the model (for example a class the preflight could not detect): those cells get no categorical contribution, which is how maxent.jar treats a class without training data.
  2. Continuous-variable extrapolation — if any continuous variable's projection range exceeds its training range (Elith, Kearney & Phillips 2010), the dialog reports the affected variables and the magnitude of the excursion.

Click Yes to proceed; No aborts the projection so you can revise the input rasters.

docs.title: After the projection
docs.text:
A success message appears in the panel:

The GeoTIFF is loaded into QGIS with a default white-to-green ramp keyed to the cloglog 0–1 range, ready to compose into a publication map.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Move to the ⑤ Survey Site Selection tab to turn the suitability raster into a field-ready layer of candidate survey sites, or skip ahead to Exporting results to learn what is in the output workbook.

docs.title: Saving and reusing models
docs.text: Persisting a trained model and loading it back later — with confidence that variables map to rasters correctly — is what enables collaboration, re-projection onto updated environmental data, and long-term reproducibility of published QMaxent results.

docs.title: Saving a trained model
docs.text:
Every successful Maxent run writes a model.pkl file to the path you specified on the ② Parameters tab (default <project>/qmaxent_output/model.pkl). This is a Python pickle of the trained elapid.MaxentModel instance — it carries:

  • The fitted regularized-likelihood coefficients
  • The complete list of variable names (in order)
  • For each variable: type (continuous / categorical), training data range (continuous) or class set (categorical)
  • The full set of hyperparameters (feature classes, RM, CV scheme, random seeds)
  • A QMaxent build-version stamp

Treat the .pkl as the canonical record of the trained model. Distribute it alongside the results.xlsx workbook when sharing with collaborators or publishing supplementary material — that is the pair of files Araújo et al. 2019 cite as the minimum reproducibility unit for a published SDM.

docs.title: Model card and coefficient table
docs.text:
Since v0.2.0, QMaxent writes two plain-text files next to the .pkl, named after it (for model.pkl: model_model_card.json and model_coefficients.csv):

File Contents <model>_model_card.json Software versions (QMaxent, elapid); settings (feature classes and whether Auto or Manual selection chose them, regularization multiplier, output transform, hinge and threshold knots, CV method and folds, random seed, permutation-importance evaluation data); data summary (presence and background counts, each variable with its type, training range and raster file); performance (training AUC, per-fold and mean CV AUC); thresholds (MTP, T10, MaxSSS); variable importance (permutation and jackknife); model constants <model>_coefficients.csv One row per Maxent feature: index, feature type (linear, quadratic, product, threshold, hinge, categorical), variable, a short description, the knot value for hinge and threshold features, the fitted coefficient, and whether it is non-zero

Use the model card to report the run in a methods section or a supplement, and the coefficient table to see which features the regularization kept. Unlike the .pkl, both files are safe to open and share: they contain only text and numbers, no executable code.

docs.title: Reloading a saved model
docs.text: On the ① Data tab, click Load existing model (.pkl)… and select the saved file. QMaxent reads the variable list out of the pickle and opens a variable-mapping dialog:

docs.title: Step 1. Click Load existing model
docs.text: 1. On the ① Data tab, click Load existing model (.pkl)... and choose the .pkl file.

docs.title: Step 2. Match each model variable to a raster
docs.text:
1. For every variable the model was trained with, choose the raster layer that holds it now.
  2. Click Load model. The raster list is rebuilt in the model's order and you can go straight to ④ Results → Spatial Projection.

The dialog has one row per saved variable. For each row, QMaxent picks a default raster from the current QGIS project by matching variable names to layer names. When the names match exactly, the dialog is just a confirmation step. When they differ, the dialog forces an explicit mapping — the only way to load a .pkl whose variable names do not match the current naming convention is to consciously re-state which raster maps to which saved variable.

This safeguard prevents the silent ordering errors that have been documented as a recurring source of "but it worked yesterday" bugs in collaborative SDM projects.

docs.title: The variable-mapping dialog in detail
docs.text:
The dialog renders three columns:

  • Saved variable name — read from the pickle, not editable.
  • Type — continuous or categorical, also from the pickle. A variable saved as categorical can only be mapped to a raster the current project has marked as categorical.
  • Mapped raster — a drop-down listing the rasters in the current project. Pick one for each row.

A footer status line reads 0 of N mapped and updates live as you populate the drop-downs. The OK button enables only when all rows are mapped.

After confirmation, QMaxent rewires the dock as if you had just trained the model fresh — the ③ Training tab is skipped and ④ Results is enabled directly. You can immediately run a spatial projection or select survey sites against the new raster stack.

docs.title: Re-projecting onto an updated raster stack
docs.text:
The most common reason to reload a model is to apply it to a more recent or higher-resolution version of the same environmental layers without re-fitting. Because re-fitting on different rasters would produce a different model, this is the only correct way to ask "what does the original model predict about the new data?".

The workflow:

  1. Train the model once on the original rasters; save model.pkl.
  2. Load the new raster stack into QGIS.
  3. Load existing model (.pkl)…, map saved variables to the new rasters in the dialog, click OK.
  4. Switch to ④ Results → Spatial Projection and run.

The preflight dialog will flag any extrapolation introduced by the new data — particularly important when the new rasters extend the geographic extent or include time periods outside the original training range.

docs.title: Security note on Python pickle files
docs.text:
.pkl files are Python pickles, which can contain executable code. Loading a malicious .pkl can run arbitrary code on your machine. Only open .pkl files that you produced yourself or that come from trusted collaborators. The model card (.json) and the coefficient table (.csv) are safe to share and open.

QMaxent has no way to verify the provenance of a third-party .pkl beyond what Python's pickle module itself does (which is nothing). For published QMaxent results, the safe pattern is:

  • Distribute the model.pkl alongside the results.xlsx workbook and the model card so reviewers have the deterministic seed, hyperparameters, and inputs needed to re-train an equivalent model from scratch if they prefer not to load the pickle. The model card and coefficient table let them inspect the model without opening the pickle at all.
  • Sign the .pkl with a SHA-256 hash in your supplementary materials.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: The companion document is Exporting results, which describes the multi-sheet XLSX workbook that ships alongside every model.pkl.

docs.title: ③ Training tab
docs.text: When you click ▶ Run Maxent at the bottom of the dock, focus shifts to the Training tab. A progress bar shows fold-by-fold progress and a log panel records what the model is doing in real time — useful for diagnosing slow runs, oversized rasters, or convergence issues.

docs.title: Step 1. Start the run and follow it
docs.text:
Click ▶ Run Maxent at the bottom of the dock. The dock switches to this tab.

  1. The progress bar.
  2. The current step, for example the jackknife model being fitted.
  3. The log. Every step is written here as it happens.

docs.title: Step 2. Read the summary
docs.text:
1. The status line reports that the run is finished.
  2. The end of the log summarises the model and the evaluation (see Reading the log).
  3. The bottom line of the dock keeps the key numbers: the number of presence and background points, the training AUC and the cross-validated AUC.

docs.title: Step 3. Keep a copy of the log
docs.text:
1. Clear log empties the log window.
  2. Copy log copies the whole log to the clipboard.
  3. Save log as... saves the log as a text file, which is useful as a record of the run.

docs.title: What happens when you click Run
docs.text:
QMaxent runs the following pipeline; each step writes a status line to the log:

flowchart TD
    A["Sample background points"] --> B["Extract raster covariates<br/>(presence + background)"]
    B --> C["Apply maxnet auto-rule<br/>(or your manual feature choice)"]
    C --> D["Fit full Maxent model"]
    D --> E["Compute training ROC + AUC"]
    E --> F["Run spatial K-Fold CV<br/>(repeat fit per fold)"]
    F --> G["Compute pooled CV AUC"]
    G --> H["(optional) Jackknife loop:<br/>2N additional fits"]
    H --> I["Save .pkl, model card, coefficients<br/>+ results.xlsx"]

The fit is performed by elapid's MaxentModel, a faithful Python port of the original Java MaxEnt (Phillips et al. 2006; Phillips et al. 2017) that delegates the regularized likelihood maximisation to scikit-learn (Pedregosa et al. 2011). The result is numerically very close to Java MaxEnt for identical inputs and identical hyperparameters — the residual difference comes mostly from how each implementation handles ties in the optimisation step.

docs.title: Reading the log
docs.text:
A typical successful run produces a log like:

→ 10,000 background points sampled
Extracting raster covariates for presence points…
Extracting raster covariates for background points…
→ Presence: 116, Background: 10,104
→ Feature types: ['linear', 'quadratic', 'product', 'hinge']
Training MaxentModel…
→ Model training complete
→ Model saved: …/model.pkl
Computing ROC curve…
→ Training AUC = 0.9569
Running cross-validation…
  Fold 1: 22 test presences, AUC = 0.7453
  Fold 2: 21 test presences, AUC = 0.7839
  Fold 3: 39 test presences, AUC = 0.8097
  Fold 4: 26 test presences, AUC = 0.8614
  Fold 5:  8 test presences, AUC = 0.5903
→ CV AUC = 0.7436 ± 0.0750  (n=5 fold(s))

A few patterns to recognise:

  • Presences dropped (⚠ N of M presence points fall outside the rasters or on NoData cells and were excluded.): the log now says how many presence points were lost and why. A large share usually means a CRS problem or rasters that do not cover the study area.

  • Presences sharing a raster cell (ℹ N presence point(s) share a raster cell with another presence.): two or more records fall in the same cell of the first raster. maxent.jar removes such duplicates by default; QMaxent keeps them, so they count more than once in the fit. If this is not intended, thin the records spatially before modeling (Boria et al. 2014).

  • Background = 10,104 (background + presence-added rows) — points that fell on NoData cells were dropped. Normal and not a cause for concern unless the loss is large (>5 %).

  • Per-fold AUC well below the mean — for example Fold 5 above (AUC = 0.59 with only 8 presences). Geographic K-Fold deliberately produces uneven folds, and a small fold can land on an atypical region of the study area. The pooled mean smooths this out.
  • Train AUC ≫ CV AUC — the spatial-CV gap. A good sign in the sense that it tells you the model has not been silently over-fitted to the training presences (Roberts et al. 2017). A train AUC of 0.95 with a CV AUC of 0.55 is the warning sign — the CV is telling you the model does not generalise.

docs.title: Completion
docs.text:
When the run finishes, you see the green Done state:

The dock's footer status bar populates with train AUC=… CV AUC=… and the ④ Results tab unlocks.

docs.title: Cancelling a run
docs.text: Click Cancel to abort. QMaxent terminates the current fold cleanly, discards the in-memory model, and leaves disk outputs untouched. You can restart by clicking ▶ Run Maxent again.

docs.title: Common warnings
docs.text: Message Meaning Action ⚠ 12 of 116 presence points fall outside the rasters or on NoData cells and were excluded. Some points fell outside the rasters or on NoData cells Inspect the raster stack; may indicate the wrong CRS or a clipped raster ℹ 3 presence point(s) share a raster cell with another presence. Duplicate records at the raster resolution are kept Thin the presences if the duplicates are not intended ⚠ Background points cap reduced from 10,000 to N Study area too small for the requested background size Reduce the background-points field on Data tab ⚠ Convergence not reached after 500 iterations Hard-to-fit model (often very few presences) Increase the regularization multiplier or simplify the feature set

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Move to the ④ Results tab to inspect response curves, Jackknife importance, and run a spatial projection.

docs.title: Worked examples
docs.text: Three end-to-end case studies, each highlighting a different aspect of QMaxent and a different real-world workflow.

docs.title: Overview of the examples
docs.text:
Example Species Highlights What you will learn Bradypus variegatus Three-toed sloth Bundled dataset; 8 bioclimatic variables + biome, 116 presences The complete QMaxent feature tour — same workflow as the original Maxent paper Ariolimax Pacific banana slug Mismatched rasters The Check Raster Consistency + Harmonize to Folder… preflight Pitta nympha Fairy pitta Reproduction of Lee et al. 2025 How to reproduce a published study in QMaxent and compare results with maxent.jar on identical inputs

The three examples are designed to be completed in order: Bradypus introduces the workflow, Ariolimax adds raster harmonisation, Pitta nympha adds publication-quality reproduction with academic comparison.

docs.title: How to follow along
docs.text:
Every example assumes you have completed Installation and that the QMaxent environment ready banner is green.

Two of the three datasets are bundled with the plugin — load them via Plugins → QMaxent → Download Example Dataset → \<species name>:

  • Bradypus variegatus: 9 variables (8 bioclimatic variables and a categorical biome raster), 116 presences, ships with the plugin. Bit-identical to the Phillips et al. 2006 dataset as distributed with the R package dismo.
  • Ariolimax — 6 variables, 3,732 presences, the elapid library's default Pacific-coast slug dataset. The official download is pre-harmonised — to follow the Ariolimax worked example exactly, you will need to use the deliberately desynchronised version described in the example's header.
  • Pitta nympha: 10 variables (2 categorical), 47 nests in Geoje-si, South Korea. Sourced from the supplementary archive of Lee et al. 2025; not bundled with the plugin (licence considerations).

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: All three examples are run with fixed random seeds. Since v0.2.0 the seed also fixes the background sample, so with the same inputs, the same raster order and the same settings, a run reproduces the same numbers. Some screenshots and numbers in the Bradypus and Ariolimax chapters were recorded with v0.1.x (LQPHT under Auto, unseeded background) and differ slightly from what v0.2.0 gives; those places are marked.

docs.title: Ariolimax
docs.text: The Pacific banana slug Ariolimax columbianus is the second worked example. Its purpose is different from Bradypus's feature tour — this dataset is deliberately messy: the supplied environmental rasters do not share a common CRS, extent, or resolution. The example walks through QMaxent's Check Raster Consistency preflight and Harmonize to Folder… workflow, showing the silent-failure mode you would otherwise hit and the one-click fix that makes the data Maxent-ready.

docs.title: 1. Dataset
docs.text:
The Ariolimax dataset is the default that ships with elapid. It comes in two variants chosen via the Download Example Dataset dialog:

  • Pre-harmonized (default) — the same six rasters already reprojected and resampled onto a common grid. Use this if you want to jump straight to model fitting.
  • Mismatch demo — the original tiles with their original CRS, extent, and resolution intact. Use this if you want to exercise the Check + Harmonize tooling.

This walkthrough uses the Mismatch demo variant. After clicking Download, the layers appear on the QGIS canvas spanning California's coastal range:

Visually the data already looks unified. The raster tiles, however, were authored by different remote-sensing pipelines and inherit different projections and resolutions — exactly the situation that breaks Maxent silently.

docs.title: 2. The mismatch problem
docs.text:
Open Plugins → QMaxent → QMaxent Analysis. On ① Data, choose the ariolimax-ca presence layer (3,732 points), then Add from project to register every loaded raster (six in total — ca-cloudcover-mean, ca-cloudcover-stdv, ca-leafareaindex-mean, ca-leafareaindex-stdv, ca-surfacetemp-mean, ca-surfacetemp-stdv). Click Check Raster Consistency:

The status line turns amber and reports:

⚠ Grid mismatch — CRS, extent, resolution differ across rasters. Click "Harmonize to Folder…" to align.

Crucially, the Run Maxent button is not blocked — Maxent itself would still produce numbers. Those numbers, however, would be silently wrong: covariates would be sampled from the cells nominally underneath each presence point but actually belonging to misaligned rasters. This is the single most common silent-failure mode in operational SDM and the entire reason this preflight exists.

docs.title: 3. Running Harmonize to Folder…
docs.text:
A new button appears next to Check Raster Consistency as soon as a mismatch is detected: Harmonize to Folder…. Click it and choose an output directory. QMaxent picks the highest-resolution raster as the reference grid, reprojects every other raster to that grid via gdalwarp under the hood (nearest-neighbour for categoricals, bilinear for continuous), and writes new GeoTIFFs into the chosen folder. The new files are auto-loaded into the project and the old ones are removed from the QMaxent raster list.

The Data tab refreshes to show the harmonized stack:

The status line is now green:

✓ All 6 rasters share grid (CRS: EPSG:3857, resolution: 1258.3 × 1258.3).

Harmonized rasters get a numeric prefix (00_, 01_, …) that locks their order. This survives a .qgz save+reload cycle — the model variable order is part of the model's identity, and the prefix makes that order visible at the file-system level too.

docs.title: 4. Running the model
docs.text:
With the stack harmonized, the rest of the workflow is identical to Bradypus. Accept the defaults on ② Parameters, click ▶ Run Maxent, and let the training complete:

Numbers from an earlier version

The values in this section were recorded with QMaxent v0.1.x, which used LQPHT under Auto and drew a new background sample on every run. v0.2.0 uses LQPH for these 3,000+ presences and a seeded background, so your values will differ slightly.

The status bar at the bottom summarises: presence=3320 background=13,257 | train AUC=0.8647 | CV AUC=0.7141. Reading the log:

  • Full-data model — Training AUC = 0.8647.
  • Cross-validation — Geographic K-Fold n=5, seed=42:
Fold Test presences AUC 1 815 0.7395 2 1,039 0.6676 3 518 0.7350 4 46 0.6671 5 902 0.7611

Pooled mean ± std = 0.7141 ± 0.0392.

The much tighter ± 0.04 standard deviation (compared to Bradypus's ± 0.075) reflects Ariolimax's larger and more uniformly distributed presence sample — when each spatial fold contains hundreds rather than a handful of presences, the per-fold AUC stabilises.

docs.title: Response curve
docs.text:
ca-surfacetemp-stdv (variability of land-surface temperature) carries the strongest stand-alone signal — biologically sensible for an organism whose activity windows depend on cool, moist microclimates:

The curve shows suitability rising as temperature variability falls below ~ 2 K and dropping to near zero above ~ 8 K — the classic preference of a moisture-dependent species for thermally stable maritime climates.

docs.title: Jackknife importance
docs.text:
The Jackknife panel ranks every variable by both stand-alone power and removal cost:

ca-surfacetemp-stdv and ca-leafareaindex-mean lead, with the cloud-cover variables weakest. The "without" bars cluster tightly above 0.85 — same correlation-pattern argument as Bradypus.

docs.title: Permutation importance
docs.text: The permutation view distributes the total importance across all variables and is directly comparable to maxent.jar's per-variable percentage table:

docs.title: 6. Comparing models with and without harmonization
docs.text:
We strongly recommend running the model once on the unharmonized stack as a teaching exercise. With Maxent's permissive raster handling you will get a finished model and a finished AUC, but the AUC will typically be 0.05–0.10 higher than the harmonized run — not because the model is better, but because covariate misalignment introduces spurious patterns that the model fits to. The cross-validation gap (training vs. CV AUC) widens correspondingly.

Always run Check Raster Consistency before drawing conclusions.

docs.title: 7. Survey site selection
docs.text:
After projection, switch to ⑤ Survey Site Selection, choose High-suitability search mode, and click ▶ Select Survey Sites. The defaults work well for Ariolimax's smaller study area:

The sites land on the coastal mountain ranges that the suitability map highlighted, and survey teams can take the resulting GeoPackage straight to the field:

docs.title: What this example demonstrates
docs.text:
1. The two example variants (Pre-harmonized vs Mismatch demo) for didactic use of the same dataset.
  2. The silent-failure mode of Maxent when rasters disagree.
  3. QMaxent's preflight + harmonize tooling that turns a project-killing mistake into a one-click fix.
  4. Sample-size effects on spatial CV variability — 3,732 presences produce a tighter ± std than Bradypus's 116.

Carry the same habit into your own work: every time you assemble a new raster stack, run Check Raster Consistency before training. If it fails, harmonize first, train second.

docs.title: Bradypus variegatus
docs.text: The brown-throated three-toed sloth — Bradypus variegatus — is the canonical Maxent test dataset, originally published with Phillips, Anderson & Schapire 2006 and reused in virtually every subsequent Maxent paper. We use it here as a guided tour of every QMaxent feature: dependency setup, data loading, parameter selection, spatial cross-validation, jackknife and permutation importance, projection, and survey planning. By the end of this chapter you will have produced — and be able to defend academically — a complete Bradypus habitat-suitability model.

docs.title: 0. Before you start: dependencies
docs.text:
QMaxent installs its third-party Python libraries (elapid, rasterio, geopandas, scikit-learn, scipy, numpy, matplotlib) into an isolated package folder so they cannot conflict with QGIS's own Python (a virtual environment on Linux and macOS; on Windows, a package folder filled by the QGIS Python's own pip, see Dependencies). The first time you open the plugin, you are invited to perform a one-time install:

Click Install / Update Dependencies. The progress bar walks through the four pip phases (collecting, downloading, building, installing) and finishes with the green badge below — at that point every QMaxent feature is ready to run.

If you ever need to recreate the package folder (e.g. after a major QGIS upgrade), the Remove Environment button on the same dialog is the clean way to start over.

docs.title: 1. Dataset
docs.text:
The Phillips et al. (2006) dataset, as distributed with the R package dismo, contains 116 presences, 8 bioclimatic variables and one categorical biome raster (9 rasters in total):

Layer Type Description bradypus Vector point 116 occurrence records across South and Central America bio1, bio5, bio6, bio7, bio8 Continuous raster Temperature variables (WorldClim) bio12, bio16, bio17 Continuous raster Precipitation variables (WorldClim) biome Categorical raster Biome type (Olson et al. 2001)

All rasters share the same grid: EPSG:4326, 0.5° × 0.5° cells, full Americas coverage. Total dataset size < 100 MB.

Download via Plugins → QMaxent → Download Example Dataset, pick Bradypus variegatus (Phillips et al, 2006 standard), choose a destination folder, and click Download:

Layers are added to the QGIS project automatically:

docs.title: 2. Loading data into the Analysis dock
docs.text:
Open Plugins → QMaxent → QMaxent Analysis. On ① Data, pick bradypus from the Presence Points Layer drop-down — QMaxent immediately reports 116 presence points loaded.

Click Add from project to register every loaded raster at once. The biome row gets a [categorical] tag (its sidecar metadata says so). Click Check Raster Consistency to verify the grid; the status line should read ✓ All 9 rasters share grid (CRS: EPSG:4326, resolution: 0.5 × 0.5), exactly what you expect from the bundled dataset:

Background Points is left at its default of 10,000, the value Phillips & Dudík 2008 recommend for continental extents. The Export for external Maxent panel at the bottom is optional — leave it alone for this tutorial; see Exporting results for when it matters.

docs.title: 3. Model setup
docs.text:
Switch to ② Parameters. For this tour we accept every default — each default is the literature-recommended value, and accepting them lets us inspect what those choices produce:

  • Feature Types: Auto (maxnet default rule by sample size). The maxnet default (Phillips et al. 2017) gives LQPH (linear, quadratic, product, hinge) for 80 or more presences, so LQPH for 116 presences. Threshold features are not added automatically (see ② Parameters tab).
  • Regularization multiplier: 1.0 (Phillips & Dudík 2008 recommendation).
  • Spatial evaluation: Geographic K-Fold (Anderson 2023), 5 folds, grid 50,000 m, buffer 50,000 m, Fix random seed = 42 (Roberts et al. 2017 default). Since v0.2.0 the seed also fixes the background sample.
  • Jackknife variable importance: enabled.
  • Permutation importance: enabled, 10 repeats, Evaluate on: Training data (maxent.jar convention).
  • Output files: qmaxent_output/model.pkl and qmaxent_output/results.xlsx.

The fixed random seed means anyone re-running this tutorial gets bit-identical results — central to computational reproducibility (Araújo et al. 2019).

docs.title: 4. Running training and cross-validation
docs.text:
Click ▶ Run Maxent. The ③ Training tab takes over and finishes in about 30 seconds:

Numbers from an earlier version

The AUC values and fold sizes in this section were recorded with QMaxent v0.1.x, which used LQPHT under Auto and drew a new background sample on every run. With v0.2.0 (LQPH, seeded background) your values will differ slightly; the interpretation is unchanged.

The status bar at the bottom summarises the run: presence=116 background=10,104 | train AUC=0.9569 | CV AUC=0.7436. Reading the log section by section:

  • Full-data model — Training AUC = 0.9569, saved to qmaxent_output/model.pkl.
  • Cross-validation — Geographic K-Fold n=5, seed=42:
Fold Test presences AUC 1 58 0.7779 2 20 0.7711 3 22 0.7531 4 8 0.5994 5 8 0.8165

Pooled mean ± std = 0.7436 ± 0.0750.

  • Jackknife variable importance — per-variable AUC across the same 5 folds in three modes (full-model reference, only this variable, and without this variable). The numbers feed the Jackknife plot below.
  • Permutation importance: sklearn permutation_importance with n_repeats=10, evaluated on the training data (presences and background), as maxent.jar does. Results feed the Permutation Importance sub-tab.
  • Save results: results.xlsx, training_log.txt, the model card (model_model_card.json) and the coefficient table (model_coefficients.csv) are persisted next to the .pkl.

Train AUC = 0.957 while CV AUC = 0.744 ± 0.075. That gap is the cost of holding out spatially-distinct validation sets — and a far more honest measure of real-world predictive performance than the inflated training AUC alone, exactly the point Roberts et al. 2017 make.

Folds 4 and 5 have the smallest validation set (8 presences each) and the largest spread in AUC. In spatial CV, folds are intentionally uneven in area, and one fold can land on a small, atypical region. The pooled CV AUC averages over this variance — the ± 0.075 standard deviation is precisely the quantity you would cite alongside the mean in a publication.

The full log is exportable via Save log as… at the bottom of the tab; Copy log drops it into the clipboard, handy for pasting into an issue report.

docs.title: Response curves
docs.text:
On ④ Results → Response Curves, pick bio12 (annual precipitation):

The model assigns highest suitability to the 1,500–3,500 mm/year band — the climatology of South American rainforest — with a sharp drop-off below ~800 mm. The shape combines hinge and quadratic features. Try other variables in the drop-down: smooth U- or peak-shaped curves indicate quadratic terms; angular kinks come from hinge features. (Step-shaped jumps would come from threshold features, which Auto no longer uses.)

docs.title: Jackknife importance
docs.text:
The Jackknife Importance sub-tab compares each variable's stand- alone signal against its incremental contribution. Dark bars (Only this variable) and light bars (Without this variable) tell you each variable's unique value:

For Bradypus:

  • bio7 (annual temperature range) and bio12 (annual precipitation) have the strongest stand-alone signals.
  • biome and bio6 (min temp of coldest month) come next.
  • The "without" bars are tightly bunched in the high-0.9s — Maxent recovers from removing any single variable because the climate variables are correlated. This is the textbook Phillips, Anderson & Schapire 2006 pattern.

docs.title: Permutation importance
docs.text:
The Permutation Importance sub-tab reports the same idea from a different lens: scikit-learn's permutation_importance shuffles each variable's values, measures the AUC drop, repeats 10 times, and normalises to 100% of the total. With the default Evaluate on: Training data (maxent.jar convention), the AUC drop is measured on the training presences and background, as in maxent.jar. Choose Held-out CV test folds (all folds pooled) to measure it on the CV test folds instead:

bio7 and bio12 again dominate; the permutation view distributes the total importance across all variables and, evaluated on the training data, is directly comparable to maxent.jar's per-variable percentage table.

docs.title: 6. Spatial projection
docs.text:
Switch to Spatial Projection in the same Results tab. Leave cloglog as the output transform (the Phillips et al. 2017 recommended default) and Auto-load result as QGIS layer ticked, then click ▶ Run Spatial Projection:

The map appears in QGIS with auto-styled white-to-green ramping:

The high-suitability core covers Brazil's southeastern Atlantic Forest and the Amazon basin — both well-known sloth strongholds — plus secondary patches across Central America. The model correctly identifies the unsuitability of the Andes (cold, high altitude) and the very dry Brazilian Northeast (Caatinga).

docs.title: 7. Saving outputs
docs.text:
These files are written automatically:

  • qmaxent_output/model.pkl — the serialised trained model. Reload it later from the Data tab's Load existing model (.pkl)… button or share it with trusted collaborators. Security note in Saving and reusing models.
  • qmaxent_output/model_model_card.json and qmaxent_output/model_coefficients.csv: a plain-text record of the run (software versions, settings, data, performance, thresholds, variable importance) and every Maxent feature with its coefficient. Unlike the .pkl, both are safe to share.
  • qmaxent_output/results.xlsx — the multi-sheet supplementary table containing experimental setup, variable list, CV results, jackknife, permutation, response-curve breakpoints, and threshold tables. See Exporting results for the sheet-by-sheet layout.

If you ticked Save analysis charts as PNG before projection, four additional 300-dpi PNGs of the response curves, ROC, jackknife, and permutation panels are written next to the GeoTIFF — sized for direct paste into a single-column manuscript figure.

docs.title: 8. Survey site selection
docs.text: A natural next step is to use the trained model to plan follow-up surveys. ⑤ Survey Site Selection offers two modes: High-suitability search (looking for new populations) and Gradient-stratified sampling (field checks across the suitability gradient). See ⑤ Survey Site Selection for all settings.

docs.title: 8.1 High-suitability search
docs.text:
High-suitability search samples sites from a high-suitability band. Open the tab, keep High-suitability search as the mode, leave the automatic Minimum suitability (0.9 × the raster maximum) and Sampling order: Random, keep 20 sites and the 1,000 m / 500 m spacing defaults, and click ▶ Select Survey Sites:

20 sites (red dots) appear on the suitability map as the layer Survey sites (survey_sites.gpkg), with their attribute table populated by OpenStreetMap reverse geocoding. With the default Address language: Local names, the addresses are in the local language of each country (Spanish or Portuguese across most of the Bradypus range):

Each site is at least 1 km from any known occurrence and at least 500 m from any other site, so a single field trip can plausibly cover several at once. High-suitability search is the right mode when the question is "where could the species be that we have not yet looked?"

docs.title: 8.2 Gradient-stratified sampling
docs.text:
Switching the Survey purpose to Gradient-stratified sampling draws a different kind of sample. A threshold (T10 by default; MTP, MaxSSS or a custom value are also offered) only defines the sampling frame. The cells above it are split into four suitability quartiles, and the same number of sites is drawn from each (Rhoden et al. 2017). No binary map is produced. A field trip can then test whether the species is found more often where the model predicts higher suitability, rather than visiting only the high-suitability core:

The resulting sites span low- through high-suitability cells in roughly equal numbers, each tagged with its quartile in the attribute table:

Gradient-stratified sampling is the right mode for checking the model in the field rather than for discovery: it is the field-side complement of the cross-validation AUC we computed in § 4.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• The same workflow with messy rasters: Ariolimax example starts from rasters that do not share a CRS or resolution — exercising the Check + Harmonize tools.
  • Compare your workflow to a published study: Pitta nympha example reproduces a published Java MaxEnt analysis in QMaxent and discusses where the two pipelines agree and differ.
  • Deeper theory: Methodological background explains why each default we accepted in this tour is the right choice.

docs.title: Pitta nympha
docs.text:
The fairy pitta Pitta nympha is a long-distance migratory passerine that breeds in dense, multi-strata broadleaved forest. The dataset used here comes from a published field study, Lee et al. (2025, Global Ecology and Conservation 64:e03939), which surveyed nest sites on Geoje Island (Geoje-si, South Korea), selected Maxent settings with ENMeval and fitted the final model with linear, quadratic and hinge features (LQH) and a regularization multiplier of 4. Re-running the same data in QMaxent serves two purposes:

  1. Worked example for real, small-n field data (47 nest locations) with a mix of continuous topographic and forest-structure variables and two categorical variables.
  2. Cross-implementation comparison with maxent.jar on identical inputs, at the default regularization (β = 1) and at the settings of Lee et al. (β = 4). See § 7 below.

docs.title: 1. Dataset
docs.text:
The ten covariates are those of Lee et al. (2025, Table 1):

Layer Type Description pitta_nympha_occurrence Vector point 47 nest locations on Geoje Island TWI Continuous raster Topographic wetness index TIN Continuous raster Elevation ASPECT Continuous raster Aspect SLOPE Continuous raster Slope (°) SMI Continuous raster Soil moisture index DBH Continuous raster Mean trunk diameter at breast height HEIGHT Continuous raster Mean tree height AGE Categorical raster Forest age class CANOPY_COVER Continuous raster Canopy closure (%) SPECIES Categorical raster Dominant tree species (class code)

All ten rasters share a common grid (EPSG:5186 KGD2002 / Central Belt, 10 m × 10 m). This is real survey data: the dataset is not bundled with the plugin's Example Dataset Downloader; the corresponding author of the manuscript holds the canonical copy (contact bhyu@knps.or.kr).

docs.title: 2. Loading data
docs.text:
On ① Data, pick pitta_nympha_occurrence from the Presence Points Layer drop-down (47 points), add all ten rasters from the project, mark AGE and SPECIES as [categorical], and click Check Raster Consistency:

The status line reads ✓ All 10 rasters share grid (CRS: EPSG:5186, resolution: 10 × 10). The presence points cluster on Geoje Island's central forested ridges:

Keep the raster order unchanged between runs: background points are drawn from the first raster in the list, so the order is part of what makes a run reproducible.

docs.title: 3. Lee-matched parameters
docs.text:
On ② Parameters, switch to Manual selection for Feature Types and tick Linear, Quadratic, Hinge (untick Product and Threshold). Set Regularization multiplier = 4.00. For Spatial evaluation, choose Random K-Fold (Phillips 2006) with Folds = 10, and leave Fix random seed on with the value 42. Leave Jackknife and Permutation importance enabled (10 repeats, Evaluate on: Training data (maxent.jar convention)):

This is the configuration that ENMeval selected in Lee et al. (2025). Note that Auto (maxnet default rule by sample size) would also give LQH for 47 presences (15 to 79 presences); the manual selection makes the choice explicit. Lee et al. evaluated the final model with ten random 75/25 splits of the presences; random 10-fold CV is the closest option in QMaxent.

docs.title: 4. Training
docs.text:
Click ▶ Run Maxent. The Training tab finishes in ~ 20 seconds:

With the fixed seed, QMaxent v0.2.0 uses 47 presences and 9,384 background points. With v0.2.0:

  • Full-data model: training AUC = 0.8645.
  • Cross-validation: Random K-Fold n=10, seed=42, CV AUC = 0.812 ± 0.110 (mean ± SD across folds). The per-fold AUCs spread widely, reflecting the small sample (4–5 test presences per fold) typical of field-survey datasets.

The table below shows how the CV AUC depends on the regularization multiplier and on the partition (QMaxent v0.2.0, mean ± SD across folds):

β Random 10-fold Geographic 5-fold 1 0.805 ± 0.108 0.713 ± 0.138 4 0.812 ± 0.110 0.739 ± 0.134

Geographic folds give lower AUCs than random folds, as expected when the test presences are spatially separated from the training presences (Roberts et al. 2017). The stronger regularization of β = 4 helps slightly under both partitions.

docs.title: Jackknife with a categorical variable
docs.text:
The log can surface a diagnostic that does not appear in the Bradypus / Ariolimax runs:

only-* skipped: dummy-column workaround produced a near-random model (train AUC = 0.531); maxnet's lasso regularisation collapsed the OneHot weights. Lower the regularization multiplier or read importance from the without-* row.

In the only-this-variable jackknife pass a categorical variable such as AGE must be one-hot encoded, but at β = 4 the L1 lasso penalty can collapse every OneHot weight back to near-zero, and Maxent has nothing left to score with. QMaxent detects this collapse, skips the affected only-* row, and tells you in plain English. The without-* row remains informative and is the right place to read the variable's incremental contribution.

This is exactly the over-regularisation failure mode Merow et al. 2013 describe. A β = 1 run recovers a meaningful only-* AUC.

docs.title: Response curve — ASPECT
docs.text: The model assigns highest suitability to north-facing aspects (roughly 270°–360°), consistent with the fairy pitta's known preference for shaded, cool, humid microclimates on ridge shoulders.

docs.title: Jackknife importance
docs.text: ASPECT, TWI, and SPECIES carry the strongest without-row signals: removing them costs the most. A skipped only-* bar means the collapse described in § 4 above occurred; read that variable's without-* bar instead.

docs.title: Permutation importance
docs.text:
The permutation pass shuffles each variable in the fitted model, so it is not affected by the lasso collapse that can disable a categorical variable's only-* jackknife row, and all ten variables get a comparable percentage:

With Evaluate on: Training data (maxent.jar convention) the ranking is computed the same way as in maxent.jar and in Lee et al. (2025). TWI, ASPECT and SPECIES are the top three variables in QMaxent, in maxent.jar and in Lee et al. (2025, Table 4); see § 7.

docs.title: 6. Survey site selection
docs.text:
After projection, the ⑤ Survey Site Selection tab in High-suitability search mode produces field-trip candidates on Geoje. With Minimum suitability at its automatic value of 0.900 (0.9 × the raster maximum), Sampling order: Random, 20 sites, at least 1,000 m from known nests and at least 500 m apart, QMaxent returns a tractable list of twenty new search locations:

Reverse geocoding fills the country, province, city_county and district fields from OpenStreetMap. With Address language: Local names (the default) the names are in Korean; choose English for English names. A level that OpenStreetMap does not hold for a location is left blank. This is a one-step path from model to field-trip planning.

docs.title: 7. Comparison with maxent.jar
docs.text:
QMaxent v0.2.0 gave maxent.jar 3.4.4 and QMaxent identical inputs: the same 47 presences and the same 9,384 background points (sampled by QMaxent with seed 42 and exported in SWD format), with LQH features. Permutation importance was evaluated on the training data in both programs.

Full-data fits on identical inputs

Setting Training AUC, maxent.jar Training AUC, QMaxent Prediction correlation (Pearson r) Permutation-importance rank agreement (Spearman ρ) β = 1 (default) 0.8795 0.8738 0.957 0.648 β = 4 (Lee et al. settings) 0.8520 0.8645 0.894 0.867 (p = 0.001)

The two programs agree closely but not to the third decimal. elapid's scikit-learn backend applies one regularization strength to all features, while maxent.jar regularizes each feature class separately, so the fitted coefficients differ somewhat. Rank agreement of the variable importances is moderate at β = 1 and strong at β = 4.

Lee et al. (2025) protocol

Following the final-model protocol of Lee et al. (LQH, β = 4, ten random 75/25 splits of the presences, identical splits in both programs), the QMaxent permutation-importance ranking agrees with Lee et al. (2025, Table 4) at Spearman ρ = 0.830. The top three variables are the same in maxent.jar, QMaxent and Lee et al.: TWI, ASPECT and SPECIES. The bias file of Lee et al. was not reproduced.

docs.title: 8. What this example demonstrates
docs.text:
1. Real-data workflow with small-n field surveys (47 presences, 10 covariates, real-world spatial scale).
  2. Categorical variable handling (AGE, SPECIES) plus the OneHot-collapse diagnostic when over-regularised.
  3. The Lee-matched (β = 4) configuration and its comparison with maxent.jar on identical inputs (§ 7).
  4. A different, narrower kind of survey site selection: a targeted search around known sub-populations rather than continental discovery.

The comparison values are recorded in tests/fixtures/pitta_golden_values.json in the QMaxent repository.

docs.title: QMaxent 매뉴얼
docs.text: QMaxent에 오신 것을 환영합니다 — QGIS 안에서 Maxent 종 분포 모델링을 가능하게 해주는 플러그인입니다. 본 매뉴얼은 첫 설치부터 발표 가능한 서식적합도 지도와 현장 조사지점 선정까지 전 워크플로를 안내합니다.

docs.title: 어디서부터 시작할까요
docs.text: 사용자 유형 추천 시작점 처음 사용 소개 → 설치 → 빠른 시작 튜토리얼 따라가기 Bradypus 예제 (전체 기능 투어) 지저분한 래스터 정리 Ariolimax 예제 (Check + Harmonize 워크플로) 발표 논문 재현 Pitta nympha 예제 (Java MaxEnt 비교) 방법론 인용 방법론 해설 → 참고문헌 문제 해결 FAQ

docs.title: 표기 관습
docs.text:
매뉴얼 전체에서 다음 관습을 사용합니다:

  • 코드 글꼴 — 파일 이름, 메뉴 항목, 명령
  • 기울임 — 종 학명과 새로운 용어
  • 굵게 — 도크 컨트롤(예: ▶ Run Maxent)
  • !!! note 블록 — 보충 정보
  • !!! tip 블록 — 권장 관행
  • !!! warning 블록 — 흔히 빠지는 함정

docs.title: 빠른 링크
docs.text:
• GitHub 저장소
  • QGIS 플러그인 페이지
  • 이슈 트래커
  • 영문 매뉴얼 (English manual)

docs.title: 인용
docs.text:
QMaxent를 활용한 연구를 발표하실 때 다음과 같이 인용해주세요:

Yu, B.-H. (2026). QMaxent: Maxent species distribution modeling in QGIS. Software. https://github.com/osgeokr/qmaxent

저장소의 CITATION.cff가 정식 출처입니다.

docs.title: Analysis 도크
docs.text: QMaxent Analysis 도크는 플러그인의 핵심으로, 전체 SDM 워크플로를 다섯 개의 번호 매겨진 탭 으로 정리해 좌에서 우로 순서대로 따라갈 수 있게 합니다. 본 장은 전체 레이아웃을 빠르게 둘러보며, 각 탭에 대한 상세 설명은 별도 장에서 다룹니다.

docs.title: 도크 열기
docs.text: 플러그인 → QMaxent → QMaxent Analysis 를 선택합니다. 도크는 기본적으로 QGIS 메인 윈도우 우측에 열리며, 표준 QGIS 패널 핸들로 분리·플로팅·재도킹할 수 있습니다.

docs.title: 다섯 탭 한눈에 보기
docs.text:
# 탭 하는 일 ① Data 종(출현 지점 레이어)과 환경 변수 래스터 선택 / 정합 확인 ② Parameters Maxent 피처 유형, 정규화, 공간 교차검증, 출력 경로 설정 ③ Training 모델 학습 진행 상황과 AUC·Jackknife·경고 로그 확인 ④ Results 반응곡선, Jackknife 변수 중요도 확인 / 공간 투영 실행 ⑤ 조사지점 선정 학습된 모델의 예측 래스터에서 현장 조사지점 선정

번호 접두어는 의도적입니다 — 순서를 명시합니다. Training 이 끝나기 전에는 Results 탭을 사용할 수 없고, 조사지점 선정 탭은 완성된 예측 래스터가 필요합니다.

docs.title: 상태바와 Run 버튼
docs.text:
어느 탭을 보고 있든 두 요소는 고정으로 유지됩니다:

  • 좌측 하단의 상태바 는 현재 모델 상태를 요약합니다(예: presence=116 background=10,104 train AUC=0.9569 CV AUC=0.7436). 학습 전에는 비어 있고, 학습 후 채워집니다.
  • 우측 하단의 큰 ▶ Run Maxent 버튼은 전체 학습+평가 파이프라인을 시작합니다. 클릭하면 자동으로 Training 탭으로 전환됩니다.

docs.title: 기존 모델 불러오기
docs.text: 처음부터 시작하지 않고 이전에 학습한 모델을 재사용하고 싶을 때가 있습니다. Data 탭 우측 상단의 Load existing model (.pkl)… 버튼은 저장된 Maxent 모델을 복원하고, 각 모델 변수를 현재 QGIS 래스터 레이어에 매핑하는 절차를 안내합니다. 전체 워크플로와 pickle 파일 보안 안내는 모델 저장 및 재사용 참고.

docs.title: 일반적인 워크플로
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[① Data] --> B[② Parameters]
    B --> C[③ Training]
    C --> D[④ Results]
    D -->|Spatial Projection| E[서식적합도 래스터]
    E --> F[⑤ 조사지점 선정]
    style C fill:#FBF7E8,stroke:#3A7E94
    style E fill:#FBF7E8,stroke:#5E8C36
다음 다섯 장에서 각 탭을 차례로 다룹니다.

docs.title: ① 데이터 탭
docs.text: 데이터 탭은 어떤 종을 모델링하고 어떤 환경 변수를 사용할지 QMaxent에 알려주는 곳입니다. 세 가지 컨트롤이 핵심입니다 — 출현 지점 선택기, Check Raster Consistency 동작이 포함된 환경 변수 래스터 목록, 배경 지점 표본 수.

docs.title: 1단계. 출현 지점 고르기
docs.text:
1. 출현 포인트 레이어에는 프로젝트의 점 레이어가 모두 나옵니다. 조사 대상 종의 레이어를 고르면 아래 회색 줄에 불러온 점의 개수가 표시됩니다.
  2. 점 파일 열기...는 점 파일(GeoPackage, 셰이프파일, GeoJSON 등 QGIS가 읽는 형식)을 프로젝트에 추가하고 바로 선택합니다.
  3. CSV 불러오기 (X/Y 열)...는 좌표 열이 있는 표를 읽습니다(2단계 참고).

docs.title: 2단계. (선택) CSV 표에서 출현 지점 불러오기
docs.text:
1. 파일: 표 파일의 경로입니다.
  2. 찾아보기...로 파일을 고릅니다.
  3. 구분자는 자동으로 찾아 줍니다. 열이 이상하게 보일 때만 바꾸세요.
  4. X / 경도 열: 경도 또는 동향 좌표 열입니다.
  5. Y / 위도 열: 위도 또는 북향 좌표 열입니다. 두 열 모두 열 이름(lon/lat, x/y 등)으로 추측해 미리 골라 둡니다.
  6. 좌표계: 표에 적힌 숫자의 좌표계입니다. 십진 경위도라면 EPSG:4326을 씁니다.
  7. OK를 누르면 표가 점 레이어로 프로젝트에 추가됩니다.

docs.title: 3단계. 환경변수 래스터 추가
docs.text:
1. 프로젝트에서 추가는 프로젝트의 래스터 레이어를 모두 목록에 넣습니다. 래스터 파일 추가...는 디스크의 래스터를 바로 추가합니다.
  2. 각 줄에는 유형 버튼이 있습니다. 기온처럼 양을 잰 값은 연속형([continuous]), 토지피복이나 biome처럼 분류 코드는 범주형([categorical])입니다. 버튼을 누르면 바뀝니다. 선택 제거와 ▲ ▼ 버튼으로 줄을 지우거나 순서를 바꿀 수 있습니다.

docs.title: 4단계. 래스터 격자 점검
docs.text:
1. 래스터 일관성 점검을 누릅니다.
  2. 상태 줄이 초록색이면 모든 래스터의 좌표계, 범위, 해상도가 같습니다. 빨간색이면 서로 다르다는 뜻이니 래스터가 맞지 않을 때를 보세요.

docs.title: 5단계. 배경점 확인
docs.text:
1. 배경점: 샘플 수는 무작위 배경점의 개수(기본 10,000개)입니다. 아래 배경 지점 절을 참고하세요.
  2. Export for external Maxent는 선택 사항입니다. 같은 자료를 Java Maxent 프로그램용으로 내보냅니다(외부 Maxent용 내보내기 참고).

여기까지 마쳤으면 ② 매개변수 탭으로 넘어갑니다.

docs.title: 출현 지점 레이어
docs.text: 첫 번째 드롭다운은 현재 QGIS 프로젝트의 모든 벡터 점 레이어를 보여줍니다. 종 출현 기록이 담긴 레이어를 선택하세요. 선택 즉시 QMaxent가 형상을 읽어 점 개수를 드롭다운 아래에 표시합니다(예: 116 presence points loaded).

docs.title: 파일에서 바로 불러오기
docs.text:
출현 자료가 아직 QGIS 프로젝트에 없다면 드롭다운 아래 두 버튼으로 바로 불러올 수 있습니다. 불러온 레이어는 프로젝트에 추가되고 출현 레이어로 자동 선택됩니다.

  • 점 파일 열기... (Open point file...): QGIS가 읽을 수 있는 모든 점 형식 (GeoPackage, Shapefile, GeoJSON, KML, GML, FlatGeobuf 등)을 엽니다. 점이 없는 레이어는 거부합니다.
  • CSV 불러오기 (X/Y 열)... (Load CSV (X/Y columns)...): 경도/위도 또는 X/Y 열이 있는 표(CSV, TXT, TSV)를 점 레이어로 만듭니다. 파일을 고르면 구분자(쉼표, 세미콜론, 탭, 파이프)와 좌표 열을 자동으로 찾습니다. GBIF 내려받기 자료의 decimalLongitude / decimalLatitude 열도 인식합니다. 결과가 맞지 않으면 구분자, X / 경도 열, Y / 위도 열 을 직접 고치세요. 좌표계 는 기본 EPSG:4326(십진 경위도)이며, 투영 좌표 표라면 해당 좌표계를 선택합니다.

이 레이어 준비 시 팁:

  • 형상은 Point 또는 MultiPoint 여야 합니다.
  • 좌표계는 QGIS가 지원하는 어떤 CRS도 가능 — QMaxent가 내부적으로 래스터의 좌표계로 재투영합니다.
  • 같은 셀의 출현점: maxent.jar는 같은 래스터 셀에 떨어진 출현점을 기본으로 하나만 남기지만 QMaxent는 모두 유지합니다. ③ 학습 탭 로그가 그런 점의 개수를 알려 주므로, 의도한 것이 아니라면 학습 전에 공간 솎아내기 (spatial thinning)로 정리하세요. 같은 좌표의 중복 기록은 벡터 → 지오프로세싱 도구 → 중복 형상 제거 로도 지울 수 있습니다.
  • 대용량 출현점: 수십만 개 규모의 출현점은 대부분 같은 셀의 중복이며, 모델 적합 한 번에 수 GB의 메모리가 필요합니다(시험 결과 10만 개에서 약 4 GB). 먼저 셀당 하나로 줄이거나 공간 솎아내기를 하세요. 점유 셀이 한 번씩만 반영되면 모델은 거의 달라지지 않습니다.
  • 공간 필터링: 부분 영역만 모델링하려면 미리 해당 영역으로 잘라낸 레이어를 추가하세요.

docs.title: 환경 변수 래스터 목록
docs.text:
아래 큰 목록 패널이 모델이 사용할 모든 래스터를 담습니다. 버튼으로 관리:

  • Add from project – 현재 프로젝트의 모든 래스터 레이어를 한 번에 추가. bioclim 변수가 가득한 폴더를 드래그한 직후 가장 빠른 방법.
  • 래스터 파일 추가... (Add raster files...) – GDAL이 읽을 수 있는 단일 밴드 래스터(GeoTIFF, ESRI ASCII(.asc), .grd, ERDAS .img, VRT, NetCDF 하위 데이터셋 등)를 골라 QGIS 프로젝트와 이 목록에 함께 추가.
  • Remove selected – 선택된 항목 제거.
  • ▲ / ▼ – 래스터 순서 변경. 결과 XLSX의 컬럼 순서에 영향을 주므로 의미있게 정렬해 두면 좋습니다. 배경점은 목록의 첫 래스터 에서 뽑으므로, 같은 시드로 결과를 똑같이 재현하려면 순서를 바꾸지 마세요.

래스터 목록은 QGIS 프로젝트를 따라갑니다. 레이어 패널에서 래스터를 제거하면 이 목록에서도 빠지고, 상태 줄이 래스터 일관성 점검을 다시 실행하라고 알려 줍니다.

다중 밴드 래스터

QMaxent는 환경변수 하나에 래스터 밴드 하나를 씁니다. 밴드가 여러 개인 래스터가 목록에 있으면 ▶ Run Maxent 를 눌렀을 때 실행을 멈추고 해당 래스터를 알려 줍니다. 먼저 프로세싱 > GDAL > 래스터 변환 > 밴드 재배열 (Rearrange bands)로 밴드마다 파일 하나씩 저장한 뒤, 단일 밴드 파일을 추가하세요.

각 래스터 우측에 [continuous] / [categorical] 토글이 있습니다. 범주형 래스터는 반드시 categorical로 표시하세요 — QMaxent는 이를 one-hot 인코딩하며, 범주형을 연속으로 처리하면 무의미한 결과를 만듭니다. 토지피복 분류 인덱스, 토양 유형, 생물군계 ID 같은 변수가 여기 해당됩니다.

Bradypus 예제 데이터를 불러오고 biome 을 categorical로 표시한 뒤:

docs.title: Check Raster Consistency
docs.text:
QMaxent의 조용한 오류 차단기 입니다. 모든 래스터가 동일한 좌표계, 범위, 해상도 를 공유하는지 검증합니다. Maxent는 정합되지 않은 래스터에서도 오류를 던지지 않습니다 — 오프셋 셀에서 공변량을 표본화해 단지 잘못된 예측을 만들 뿐입니다. 래스터 목록을 변경할 때마다 이 검사를 실행하시길 강력히 권장합니다.

가능한 결과:

상태 의미 ✓ All rasters share grid (CRS, resolution) 진행 가능 ⚠ CRS mismatch 또는 extent mismatch Harmonize Rasters 사용 (다음 절) ⚠ Resolution mismatch Harmonize Rasters 로 공통 그리드로 리샘플 ⚠ 래스터 N개의 좌표계(CRS)에 문제가 있습니다 좌표계를 먼저 지정해야 함 (아래 안내 상자)

검사가 통과하면 결과·공유 좌표계·해상도가 버튼 아래 상태 줄에 기록됩니다 — 프로젝트 저장·재로드 후에도 유지되는 정합성 체크입니다.

검사가 실패했을 때의 흐름은 Ariolimax 실전 예제 참고.

쓸 수 없는 좌표계

래스터 일관성 점검 (Check Raster Consistency)은 다른 좌표계로 변환할 수 없는 래스터를 파일명과 함께 알려 줍니다. 흔한 경우는 두 가지입니다:

  • 좌표계 정보가 아예 없는 래스터
  • datum이 없는 로컬(engineering) 좌표계. 예를 들어 .prj 에 "NAD83(NSRS2007) / Michigan South" 같은 이름만 있고 datum 정보가 없으면 PROJ는 이를 다른 좌표계로 변환할 수 없습니다.

좌표계 이름이 EPSG 좌표계 하나와 정확히 일치하면 안내창이 맞는 EPSG 코드를 함께 제안합니다. 해결하려면 레이어 패널에서 해당 래스터를 우클릭하고 레이어 좌표계 > 레이어 좌표계 설정... 에서 올바른 좌표계(예: 제안된 EPSG 코드)를 고른 뒤 점검을 다시 실행하세요. 이렇게 설정한 좌표계는 점검과 Harmonize 모두에 반영됩니다. 좌표계 정보를 완전하게 담아 래스터를 다시 저장해도 됩니다.

docs.title: 래스터가 맞지 않을 때
docs.text: 아래 단계는 예제 데이터의 Ariolimax Mismatch demo를 사용합니다. 래스터 격자를 일부러 바꿔 둔 사본입니다.

docs.title: 1단계. 래스터를 넣고 점검하기
docs.text:
1. 출현 레이어를 고릅니다.
  2. 프로젝트에서 추가로 래스터를 넣습니다.
  1. 래스터 일관성 점검을 누릅니다.
  2. 격자가 서로 다르므로 폴더에 정합... 버튼이 새로 나타납니다. 이 버튼을 누릅니다.
  3. 빨간 상태 줄에 무엇이 다른지(좌표계, 범위, 해상도) 표시됩니다.

docs.title: 2단계. 저장 폴더를 고르고 정합하기
docs.text: QMaxent가 결과를 저장할 폴더를 묻습니다. 첫 래스터 옆의 qmaxent_harmonized 폴더가 미리 선택되어 있으니 폴더 선택을 누르면 됩니다. 원본 파일은 바뀌지 않습니다. 이어서 진행 창이 나타납니다.

docs.title: 3단계. 목록의 래스터 바꾸기
docs.text:
1. 교체를 누르면 원본 대신 정합된 사본을 씁니다. 추가 레이어로 추가는 두 세트를 모두 프로젝트에 남깁니다.
  1. 목록이 정합된 사본을 가리킵니다.
  2. 상태 줄이 초록색으로 바뀝니다. 이제 ② 매개변수 탭으로 넘어가면 됩니다.

내부적으로는 gdalwarp를 사용하며, 연속형 래스터는 bilinear, 범주형 래스터는 nearest-neighbour로 리샘플링합니다. 좌표계 문제로 정합할 수 없는 래스터가 있으면 PROJ 오류 원문 대신 위 안내 상자와 같은 메시지(파일명, 원인, 해결 방법)를 보여 줍니다.

docs.title: 배경 지점
docs.text:
Maxent는 실제 부재 지점을 필요로 하지 않습니다 — 대신 배경 지점 으로 가용 환경 공간을 표본화합니다. 기본값 10,000은 Phillips et al. (2017)의 권장값이며 거의 모든 연구에서 잘 작동합니다.

기본값 변경이 필요한 경우:

  • 작은 연구 영역 (단일 유역, 섬): 10,000개의 고유 셀이 없을 수 있음 — 5,000 또는 n_cells × 0.5 같은 작은 값 사용.
  • 대륙 또는 전 지구 모델링: 10,000으로 유지해도 무방 — 기본 maxnet 알고리즘이 잘 확장됩니다.
  • 출현 지점에 강한 공간 표본 편향: 파라미터 탭의 Down-weight spatially clustered points 옵션과 함께 사용.

상태바는 표본 후 실제 개수를 보고합니다(예: background=10,104); 요청보다 약간 작은 숫자는 NaN 셀 제외에 의한 것입니다.

배경점은 래스터 목록의 첫 래스터에서 유효한 셀을 골라 뽑습니다. ② 파라미터 탭의 랜덤 시드 고정 이 켜져 있으면 배경점 추출에도 같은 시드가 적용되어, 입력과 래스터 순서가 같으면 실행마다 같은 배경점을 얻습니다 (v0.1.x에서는 실행마다 배경점이 달랐습니다).

docs.title: 외부 Maxent용 내보내기
docs.text:
이 영역은 출현 지점과 래스터를 원래 Java 프로그램 maxent.jar가 읽는 형식으로 저장합니다. 같은 자료를 그 프로그램에서 돌려 보거나, 바로 쓸 수 있는 Maxent 입력 폴더를 공유할 때 씁니다.

  1. Export for external Maxent 영역입니다.
  2. Samples + Raster: 출현점 CSV 하나와 래스터마다 .asc 격자 파일을 씁니다.
  3. SWD: 출현점과 배경점 위치의 래스터 값을 미리 추출한 CSV 두 개를 씁니다.
  4. Output folder: 파일을 저장할 폴더입니다. ...로 바꿀 수 있습니다.
  5. Export를 누릅니다. 파일 옆에 예시 maxent.jar 명령이 담긴 README가 함께 저장됩니다.

docs.title: 기존 모델 (.pkl) 불러오기
docs.text: 우측 상단의 Load existing model (.pkl)… 버튼은 저장된 모델을 열고 각 모델 변수를 현재 QGIS 래스터에 매핑하는 절차를 안내합니다. 다른 영역으로 재투영, 두 연구 비교, 협업자와의 모델 공유에 유용합니다. 전체 절차와 pickle 파일 보안 안내 는 모델 저장 및 재사용 참고.

docs.title: 도크가 기억하는 것
docs.text: 레이어 선택과 categorical/continuous 토글은 QGIS 프로젝트(.qgs / .qgz)와 함께 저장됩니다. 프로젝트를 다시 열면 이 탭의 모든 설정이 복원되어 구성을 다시 만들지 않고도 모델링을 이어갈 수 있습니다.

docs.title: 의존성 관리
docs.text:
QMaxent의 모델링 엔진 — elapid Python 라이브러리와 동반 패키지(rasterio, geopandas, scikit-learn, matplotlib) — 는 QGIS에 기본 포함되지 않습니다. 플러그인을 처음 사용할 때, QMaxent 전용 폴더에 이 의존성들을 설치하여 시스템 Python이나 QGIS 자체에 영향을 주지 않습니다(Linux와 macOS는 격리 가상환경, Windows는 패키지 폴더. 아래 설치 위치와 방식 참고).

이는 약 5분 정도의 일회성 설정입니다.

docs.title: 1단계. QMaxent 의존성 패널 열기
docs.text:
플러그인을 설치하면 이 패널이 저절로 열립니다. 메뉴에서 언제든 다시 열 수도 있습니다.

  1. 플러그인 메뉴를 엽니다.
  2. QMaxent에 마우스를 올립니다.
  3. QMaxent 의존성을 누릅니다.

docs.title: 2단계. 의존성 설치
docs.text:
1. 환경 상태에 Dependencies not installed가 표시됩니다.
  2. 의존성 설치 / 업데이트를 누릅니다.

패키지는 PyPI에서 받아 패널 아래쪽에 표시된 경로 ~/.qgis_qmaxent(Windows는 %USERPROFILE%\.qgis_qmaxent)에 설치됩니다. 내려받는 양은 300~500 MB 정도(설치 후 약 590 MB)이고, 일반 인터넷 환경에서 3~8분 걸립니다. 기다리는 동안 버튼 아래에 진행 막대와 설치 중인 패키지 이름이 표시됩니다.

docs.title: 3단계. 준비 완료 확인
docs.text: 1. 환경 상태가 초록색 ✓ QMaxent environment ready로 바뀝니다. 패널을 닫고 QMaxent 분석을 열면 됩니다.

docs.title: 환경 상태 메시지
docs.text: 메시지 의미 ✗ Dependencies not installed 처음 한 번 설치가 필요합니다 ✓ QMaxent environment ready 모두 설치되어 모델링을 시작할 수 있습니다 ✗ Dependencies need updating 플러그인 업그레이드로 패키지 목록이나 설치 방식이 바뀌었습니다. 의존성 설치 / 업데이트를 다시 누르세요

docs.title: 설치 위치와 방식
docs.text:
설치 폴더 이름은 QGIS에 들어 있는 Python 버전을 따릅니다(예: Python 3.12이면 venv_py3.12).

운영체제 방식 설치 위치 (예) Linux, macOS 가상환경(venv)을 만들고 그 안의 pip로 설치 ~/.qgis_qmaxent/venv_py3.12/ (가상환경 폴더) Windows (v0.2.0) QGIS 자체 Python의 pip로 패키지 폴더에 설치 (pip install --target), 별도 인터프리터 없음 %USERPROFILE%\.qgis_qmaxent\venv_py3.12\Lib\site-packages

Windows 방식이 바뀐 이유: QGIS 3.44.15 이상의 Windows판에서는 가상환경 안에서 ensurepip 가 실패해("ensurepip ... returned non-zero exit status 1") 패키지를 하나도 내려받기 전에 설치가 멈췄습니다. QMaxent는 설치한 패키지를 QGIS 안에서 불러오기만 하므로 Windows에서는 가상환경 인터프리터가 필요 없습니다. v0.2.0은 QGIS 자체 pip로 QMaxent 패키지 폴더에 설치해 이 문제를 피합니다. Linux와 macOS는 기존 가상환경 방식을 그대로 씁니다.

두 환경변수로 동작을 바꿀 수 있습니다. QGIS를 시작하기 전에 설정하세요.

환경변수 효과 QMAXENT_CACHE_DIR 기본 ~/.qgis_qmaxent 대신 다른 위치에 설치 (예: 홈 폴더에 쓸 수 없거나 공간이 부족할 때) QMAXENT_FORCE_VENV=1 Windows에서도 이전(v0.1.x) 가상환경 방식을 사용

docs.title: 설치되는 패키지
docs.text:
QMaxent는 다음 패키지와 그 의존성을 설치합니다:

  • elapid — Maxent 엔진 (maxnet 알고리즘, 공간 교차검증, 투영)
  • rasterio — 래스터 입출력
  • geopandas — 출현 지점 벡터 입출력
  • scikit-learn — 교차검증, ROC, AUC
  • scipy + numpy — 수치 연산 핵심
  • matplotlib — 반응곡선, ROC, Jackknife 그래프

QMaxent가 테스트한 버전으로 핀이 고정되어 있으며, 각 릴리스 노트에 포함된 버전이 기록되어 있습니다.

docs.title: Remove Environment
docs.text:
Remove Environment 는 QMaxent 가상환경 전체를 디스크에서 삭제합니다. 다음과 같은 경우에 사용합니다:

  • QMaxent를 더 이상 사용하지 않아 디스크 공간 확보
  • 무언가 망가졌을 때 깨끗한 재설치 강제
  • 다른 패키지 버전을 핀하는 다른 QMaxent 버전으로 전환

제거 후 상태 배너는 Dependencies not installed 로 돌아가고, Install / Update Dependencies 가 다시 활성화됩니다.

docs.title: 문제 해결
docs.text:
네트워크 또는 SSL 오류로 설치 실패

대부분 회사 프록시나 방화벽이 PyPI 를 차단하기 때문입니다. 관리자에게 pypi.org 와 files.pythonhosted.org 허용을 요청하세요. 설치 도구는 QGIS의 프록시 설정을 따르므로, 설정 → 옵션 → 네트워크 를 구성하면 보통 해결됩니다.

Windows에서 'ensurepip ... returned non-zero exit status 1' 오류

v0.1.x를 QGIS 3.44.15 이상의 Windows판에서 쓸 때 생기던 오류입니다. 플러그인을 v0.2.0 이상으로 업데이트한 뒤 Install / Update Dependencies 를 다시 클릭하세요. v0.2.0은 가상환경을 만들지 않고 QGIS 자체 pip로 설치하므로 이 단계를 거치지 않습니다(설치 위치와 방식 참고). QMAXENT_FORCE_VENV=1 을 설정해 두었다면 해제하세요.

설치 중 디스크 공간 부족

설치 중에는 임시로 최종 크기의 약 두 배가 필요합니다. 홈 디렉터리가 있는 드라이브에 최소 1 GB를 확보하고 다시 시도하세요.

성공적인 설치 후에도 "No module named …" 오류

QGIS를 한 번 재시작하세요. Python의 import 캐시는 새 환경을 인식하기 위해 깨끗한 프로세스가 필요합니다.

플러그인은 시작되지만 Run Maxent 버튼이 비활성화

Dependencies 다이얼로그를 열어 상태가 초록인지 확인하세요. 초록이면 QGIS를 재시작, 그렇지 않으면 Install / Update Dependencies 를 다시 클릭하세요.

docs.title: 가상환경 보안 안내
docs.text: QMaxent의 환경은 Linux와 macOS에서는 표준 Python venv 모듈로, Windows에서는 QGIS 자체 pip의 패키지 폴더 설치로 만들어지며, 어느 경우든 PyPI에서만 설치됩니다. 플러그인은 런타임에 원격 소스의 임의 코드를 실행하지 않습니다. 저장된 모델 파일 (.pkl)은 별도의 고려사항이며, 신뢰할 수 없는 소스의 pickle을 불러올 때의 보안 주의는 모델 저장 및 재사용을 참고하세요.

docs.title: 예제 데이터
docs.text: QMaxent는 두 가지 표준 SDM 예제 데이터셋을 한 번의 클릭으로 다운로드할 수 있는 기능을 플러그인 → QMaxent → 예제 데이터셋 다운로드... 메뉴에서 제공합니다. 지난 20년간 Maxent 문헌에서 사용된 동일한 데이터셋이라, 결과를 발표 벤치마크와 직접 비교할 수 있습니다.

docs.title: 1단계. 다운로드 창 열기
docs.text:
1. 플러그인 메뉴를 엽니다.
  2. QMaxent에 마우스를 올립니다.
  3. 예제 데이터셋 다운로드...를 누릅니다.

docs.title: 2단계. 데이터셋과 저장 폴더 고르기
docs.text:
1. 데이터셋을 고릅니다. 처음이라면 Bradypus variegatus가 좋습니다.
  2. 저장 위치를 확인합니다. 기본값은 홈 폴더 아래 qmaxent_examples 폴더이며, ...를 눌러 바꿀 수 있습니다.
  3. 다운로드를 누릅니다.

Ariolimax를 고르면 Variant(변형) 선택이 함께 나타납니다.

  1. Ariolimax를 선택합니다.
  2. Variant: Pre-harmonized (default)는 공개된 래스터를 그대로, 모두 같은 격자로 불러옵니다. Mismatch demo는 좌표계, 범위, 해상도를 일부러 바꾼 사본을 불러오므로 래스터 일관성 점검을 연습할 수 있습니다 (래스터가 맞지 않을 때 참고).
  3. 저장 위치는 Bradypus와 같습니다.
  4. 다운로드를 누릅니다.

docs.title: 3단계. 다운로드 기다리기
docs.text:
1. 진행 막대와 그 아래 줄에 지금 받고 있는 파일이 표시됩니다. 멈추려면 취소를 누릅니다.

다운로드가 끝나면 파일이 저장된 위치를 알려 주는 메시지가 나타납니다.

  1. OK를 누릅니다.

docs.title: 4단계. 레이어 확인
docs.text: 1. 출현 레이어와 환경변수 래스터가 레이어 패널에 추가되고 지도에 그려집니다. 바로 빠른 시작으로 넘어가면 됩니다.

docs.title: Bradypus variegatus 데이터셋
docs.text:
세발가락나무늘보. Phillips, Anderson & Schapire (2006)와 함께 발표된 표준 Maxent 테스트 데이터셋이며, 이후 거의 모든 Maxent 논문에서 재사용된 데이터입니다.

레이어 설명 bradypus.shp 남미·중미에 분포한 116개의 출현 지점 bio1, bio5, bio6, bio7, bio8, bio12, bio16, bio17 WorldClim 생기후 변수(연속) biome 생물군계 분류(범주형)

다운로드 직후 레이어들이 QGIS 캔버스에 즉시 표시됩니다:

데이터셋은 100 MB 미만으로 작고, Maxent 학습이 보통 30초 이내에 끝나므로 첫 실행과 본 매뉴얼 학습용으로 이상적입니다.

docs.title: Ariolimax 데이터셋
docs.text:
태평양바나나민달팽이. elapid의 기본 테스트 데이터셋입니다.

Pre-harmonized와 Mismatch demo 중 무엇을 고를까요?

공개된 Ariolimax 래스터는 이미 좌표계, 범위, 해상도가 모두 같아서 래스터 일관성 점검을 바로 통과합니다. 격자가 맞지 않는 상황을 직접 보고 고쳐 보고 싶다면 Variant에서 Mismatch demo를 고르세요. Ariolimax 실전 예제와 같은 상황이 만들어집니다. 변형된 사본은 mismatch_demo 하위 폴더에 저장되며 원본 파일은 바뀌지 않습니다.

docs.title: 저장 위치 및 프로젝트 구조
docs.text:
어느 데이터셋을 선택하든 종 이름의 하위 폴더가 만들어집니다:

qmaxent_examples/
├── bradypus/
│   ├── bradypus.shp     (그리고 .dbf, .shx, .prj, .cpg)
│   ├── bio1.tif         …
│   └── biome.tif
└── ariolimax/
    ├── ariolimax.shp
    └── …

같은 저장 위치로 다이얼로그를 다시 실행하면 이전 다운로드 파일을 덮어쓰므로, 튜토리얼을 깨끗하게 다시 시작하고 싶을 때 "기본값 리셋" 버튼처럼 안전하게 사용할 수 있습니다.

docs.title: 레이어 수동 불러오기
docs.text: 플러그인이 자동으로 레이어를 추가하지만, 직접 다시 불러와야 할 경우 QGIS의 Browser 패널에서 .shp 와 .tif 파일을 Layers 패널로 드래그하면 됩니다 — 다른 데이터셋과 동일한 방식입니다.

docs.title: 데이터 출처
docs.text:
두 데이터셋 모두 다운로드 시점에 원본 아카이브 URL에서 가져옵니다 — QMaxent는 이를 플러그인 자체에 포함하지 않습니다. 이 방식은 플러그인 패키지를 작게 유지하고 항상 업스트림 표준 버전을 받을 수 있게 합니다. 오프라인 환경이 필요하다면, 인터넷이 연결된 컴퓨터에서 다운로드한 뒤 qmaxent_examples 폴더를 오프라인 워크스테이션으로 복사하세요.

두 데이터셋의 사본은 QMaxent 저장소의 example_data 폴더에도 있습니다(약 15 MB). 원본 파일을 그대로 복사했으며, 출처와 인용 정보를 담은 README.txt가 함께 들어 있습니다. 파일을 받아 레이어를 QGIS 프로젝트에 추가하면 됩니다.

docs.title: 결과 내보내기
docs.text: QMaxent 학습 실행은 매번 .pkl 모델 옆에 다중 시트 XLSX 워크북 을 작성합니다. 워크북은 의도적으로 학술 논문의 보충 표 블록 으로 읽히도록 포맷됐습니다 — Times New Roman, 표 번호 헤딩, 각 측정 지표가 어떻게 계산됐는지 설명하는 행 푸터. 시트를 논문 부록에 직접 붙여넣을 수 있습니다.

docs.title: 출력 폴더 레이아웃
docs.text:
학습 + 공간 투영 + Save analysis charts as PNG 체크박스가 켜진 실행 직후 출력 폴더는 다음과 같습니다:

파일 생성자 용도 model.pkl 학습 Load existing model (.pkl)… 로 나중에 재로드 model_model_card.json 학습 설정, 자료 요약, 성능, 임계값, 변수 중요도를 담은 모델 카드 (모델 저장 및 재사용) model_coefficients.csv 학습 모든 Maxent 피처의 유형, 변수, 기준값(knot), 계수 prediction.tif 공간 투영 서식 적합도 래스터 prediction.tif.aux 공간 투영 QGIS 보조 메타데이터 results.xlsx 학습 다중 시트 보충 표 survey_sites.gpkg 조사지점 선정 탭 현장 조사지점 prediction_roc.png 공간 투영 ROC 곡선 (300 dpi) prediction_jackknife.png 공간 투영 Jackknife 막대 (300 dpi) prediction_response_curves.png 공간 투영 모든 반응 곡선 (300 dpi)

docs.title: 시트별 설명
docs.text: XLSX는 어떤 기능을 실행했는지에 따라 4–5개 시트를 가집니다. 아래 스크린샷은 Pitta nympha 실행에서 캡처 — 형식 은 모든 데이터셋에 동일하며, 값만 변합니다.

docs.title: Table 1 — 실험 설정
docs.text:
전체 실행 구성을 한 페이지로 기록. Reviewer가 시드, 변수 수, 정규화, CV 방식, 학습/CV AUC를 한눈에 검증할 수 있습니다.

이 시트는 Methods 섹션 재현성 을 위한 단일 최고의 산출물입니다. "Table S1" 으로 인용하면 독자가 분석을 비트 단위로 재실행할 수 있습니다.

docs.title: Table 2 — 예측 변수
docs.text:
모든 환경 변수, 그 유형 (continuous / categorical), 학습 데이터 범위 나열. 연속 변수는 [min, max], 범주형은 학습 시 만난 이산적 수준 집합.

이 시트로 외삽 범위 를 문서화하세요 — 이 범위 밖의 환경 값에 적용된 어떤 예측이든 정의상 외삽이며 결과 논의에서 표시되어야 합니다.

docs.title: Table 3 — 교차검증 결과
docs.text:
Fold별 보류 AUC와 fold 사이의 평균 ± 표준편차 — 핵심 성능 추정.

degenerate 검증 셋을 가진 fold (예: 공간 분할 후 모두 양성) 는 NaN 으로 보고되며 평균에서 제외됩니다. 이는 fold가 유효한 AUC를 만들 수 없는 드문 경우를 원본 Maxent 문헌이 처리하는 방식과 일치합니다.

docs.title: Table 4 — Jackknife 변수 중요도
docs.text:
각 변수에 대해 4개의 AUC (only-train, only-test, without-train, without-test), 그리고 기여 크기를 스캔하기 쉽게 만드는 "Train AUC drop" 및 "Test AUC drop" 열. 변수는 Test AUC drop 내림차순 으로 정렬 — 가장 고유하게 정보 있는 변수가 맨 위에.

푸터 노트가 drop 열을 설명: Drop = full-model AUC − without-variable AUC; 큰 drop은 변수의 고유한 기여가 다른 변수에서 회복하기 어려움을 가리킵니다.

docs.title: 조사지점 선정 임계값과 조사지점 목록
docs.text:
워크북의 Survey Sites 시트는 ⑤ 조사지점 선정 탭의 적합도 구간별 층화 표집에 쓰는 임계값(MTP, T10, MaxSSS)을 학습 자료에서 계산해 기록합니다.

조사지점 목록 자체는 survey_sites.gpkg 에 저장됩니다. 조사지점당 한 행이며 컬럼은 id, lat, lon, suitability, quartile, 그리고 역지오코딩을 켰을 때 country, province, city_county, district, 사람이 읽을 수 있는 display_name 입니다. 주소 필드는 OpenStreetMap의 일반 행정 단위이며, 기본으로 현지 이름(각 나라의 언어)으로 기록됩니다 (⑤ 조사지점 선정 참고):

docs.title: 내보내기 커스터마이즈
docs.text:
② Parameters 탭의 기본 파일 경로는 <home>/qmaxent_output/results.xlsx 입니다. 쓰기 가능한 어떤 곳으로든 변경 가능 — 상대 경로는 현재 QGIS 프로젝트 폴더에 대해 해석됩니다.

XLSX 작성을 멈추려면 (드물지만 — 보통 파일 무시가 비활성화보다 빠름) 경로 필드를 비우면 됩니다. QMaxent는 내보내기를 건너뛰고 학습 로그에 알림을 보냅니다.

PNG 분석 차트는 ④ Results → Spatial Projection 하위 탭의 Save analysis charts as PNG 체크박스로 제어됩니다. 체크된 상태에서 투영 실행 시점에 GeoTIFF 옆에 세 개의 추가 PNG가 작성됩니다 — 단일 컬럼 원고 그림에 직접 붙여넣을 수 있는 크기 (300 dpi, 약 1.6 MB 각).

docs.title: 워크북 인용
docs.text:
